harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 successfully. inventory-api is an enabled systemd service on TCP 8080, and batchworker has a per-process 128 MiB virtual-memory limit. A 160 MiB allocation was blocked without interrupting the API. Configuration, data, firewall access, and limits survived a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Created dedicated inventoryapi and batchworker accounts.
Installed a Python 2.7-compatible inventory API with persistent data.
Enabled inventory-api.service with failure restart behavior.
Opened TCP 8080 in runtime and persistent firewalld configuration.
Applied a 131072 KiB soft and hard RLIMIT_AS to batchworker.
Rebooted node1 and verified full recovery without changing RHEL 7.9 or kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api runs as a managed service on TCP 8080
evidence.summary: Before and after reboot, systemd reported enabled/active, the inventoryapi-owned Python process listened on 0.0.0.0:8080, firewall access was persistent, and direct health/data requests succeeded.

evidence.requirement: batchworker is limited to 128 MiB virtual memory per process
evidence.summary: The effective limit was 131072 KiB. A batchworker process requesting 160 MiB received MemoryError, while the API remained healthy. The effective limit persisted after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Installed operating-system release and kernel are retained
evidence.summary: Both baseline and recovered state report RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID 0571f4dd-60b7-4601-9295-e4eebe622784, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID 3857f3dd-b0b7-4824-ac33-37c554404202, and recovered system/service/firewall/data/account-limit state.
